caption:
Whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him.

Surah At-Talaaq (65:3). Swipe through for the Arabic, then English, Mandarin, Korean, Japanese and Malay renderings.

Sources on the final slide.

sourcing.arabic: Uthmani script (edition quran-uthmani), api.alquran.cloud. Live-fetched and verified this session (2026-09-15) via GET /v1/ayah/65:3/editions/quran-uthmani,en.sahih,zh.jian,ko.korean,ja.japanese.
sourcing.english: Saheeh International (edition en.sahih), api.alquran.cloud. Same live call as above, quoted verbatim including the translator's own bracketed interpolation '[decreed]'.
sourcing.chinese: Ma Jian, 马坚 (edition zh.jian), api.alquran.cloud. Same live call as above, rendered verbatim.
sourcing.malay: Abdullah Muhammad Basmeih (edition ms.basmeih), api.alquran.cloud. Added 2026-09-15 as a permanent 6th language for the channel at the owner's explicit request. Live-fetched and verified this session via GET /v1/ayah/65:3/editions/ms.basmeih, rendered verbatim including the translator's own parenthetical interpolations.
sourcing.korean: Edition ko.korean, api.alquran.cloud. Translator is listed as 'Unknown' in the source's own metadata (englishName field), so the on-slide credit says 'translator not specified by source' rather than inventing a scholar's name. Same live call as above. The raw API string contained three stray mid-word spaces that were closed up to their correct single words for the slide: '의 탁하는' -> '의탁하는', '하나 님은' -> '하나님은', '두 셨노라' -> '두셨노라'. This is the same kind of source-data formatting artifact already documented for this edition in quran-94-5.meta.json, quran-2-152.meta.json and quran-39-53.meta.json. No wording was changed, only spacing internal to single grammatical words.
sourcing.japanese: Edition ja.japanese, api.alquran.cloud. Translator is listed as 'Unknown' in the source's own metadata, cited on-slide as 'translator not specified by source'. Same live call as above, rendered verbatim with no corrections needed.
sourcing.candidate_selection_note: The first candidate ayah considered for today (2:286) was rejected after its ko.korean rendering came back as only a 3-syllable fragment ('대가를') instead of a complete translation - re-fetched in full to rule out a display-truncation artifact, and confirmed the source data itself was incomplete for that ayah/edition pair. Rather than complete or paraphrase the missing text from memory, three alternative ayat (65:3, 14:7, 3:159) were test-fetched across all five editions, all three came back complete, and 65:3 was selected.
sourcing.verification_note: All five language renderings came from a single live api.alquran.cloud request made this session (2026-09-15), not from memory or a prior file: GET https://api.alquran.cloud/v1/ayah/65:3/editions/quran-uthmani,en.sahih,zh.jian,ko.korean,ja.japanese, HTTP 200. See channels.json's ig-blankdiscussions._niche_note for why this project treats scripture sourcing as a hard requirement, not a style choice.
sourcing.compliance_check: Manually checked against scripts/data/compliance-policy.json's halal keyword-blocklists (intoxicants, pork, gambling, riba, immodesty, profanity, superstition, origins_patterns, animate_imagery, context_review) since compliance-gate.mjs does not cover this channel's schema. No blocklisted terms present in any of the six language texts (rechecked after the Malay slide was added 2026-09-15); no imagery generated at all (pure typography slides). Content is a straightforward statement about reliance on Allah and divine provision - no context_review flags apply. Clean.
